scenario: Pin and exercise the CLI contract
interface: Unmodified az and published compatibility matrix
preconditions: A release candidate and a clean CLI configuration directory
procedure: Record the CLI version, extension versions, command arguments, API versions, and fixture image digests. Run the required matrix using that configuration.
pass_criteria: Every required command uses the selected ocean endpoints. The recorded matrix and evidence are sufficient to reproduce the run.

scenario: Inventory and supported API discovery
interface: az provider show, az group create/show/list/delete, az resource list/show
preconditions: An active subscription and enough resources to exercise pagination
procedure: Create, inspect, list, and delete a resource group and its test resources. Walk all inventory pages. Request an unsupported API version and an unsupported parameter combination.
pass_criteria: Supported requests return valid ARM IDs and complete paging. Unsupported requests return documented errors and leave resource state unchanged. Deleting the group removes its resources and releases the associated allocations.

scenario: Retries and asynchronous operation state
interface: az container create/delete, az functionapp create/delete, ARM operation polling
preconditions: A fault injector that can drop API responses and restart the controller
procedure: Run concurrent creates for the same resource ID. Drop responses after acceptance, retry the requests, and restart the controller during a create or delete. Poll the operation to completion.
pass_criteria: Each operation converges to the intended terminal state or a documented terminal error. A retry creates at most one resource and one reservation. Reads and operation status agree after convergence.

scenario: Onboard two customer tenants
interface: az rest against the ocean operator API
preconditions: An authenticated operator and a tenant-scoped test principal
procedure: Create tenants A and B with their initial subscriptions. Retry a request after a dropped response. Attempt the same operator action using the tenant principal.
pass_criteria: Each tenant has its own identity namespace and subscription. The retry preserves the original allocation. The tenant principal cannot provision other tenants.

scenario: Register the cloud and sign in
interface: az cloud register, az cloud set, az login, az account list/set/list-locations/get-access-token
preconditions: Two tenants, a test user and a service principal, empty CLI caches
procedure: Register ocean. Sign in as a user and separately as a service principal. Select a subscription, list its available locations, and obtain an access token for each supported audience.
pass_criteria: Both clients use ocean authentication. Each sees only authorized subscriptions and the correct available locations. Each token is accepted for its intended audience and rejected at unrelated endpoints.

scenario: Manage users and automation credentials
interface: az ad user create/list/show/update/delete, az ad app create, az ad sp create, az ad app credential reset --append
preconditions: A tenant administrator and scoped automation credentials
procedure: Create, read, update, and delete a test user. Create an app and service principal. Append a credential, log in with it, and verify that a valid existing credential still works.
pass_criteria: Identity changes are tenant-scoped and observable through the CLI. Deleted accounts cannot begin new sessions. Credential append preserves existing valid credentials.

scenario: Enforce resource-level roles and validate tokens
interface: az role assignment create/list/delete, az resource list/show, az rest
preconditions: A tenant administrator, a scoped service principal, and two tenant subscriptions
procedure: Grant a role at resource-group scope. Test an authorized action, out-of-scope access, cross-tenant access, and action after role removal. Submit expired, modified, wrong-audience, and wrong-issuer tokens.
pass_criteria: Only authorized actions succeed. Lists reveal no foreign resources. Denials have the documented response and leave state unchanged. Role changes and denied privileged actions are auditable.

scenario: Maintain authentication through an identity failure
interface: az login, az account get-access-token
preconditions: Redundant identity endpoints and an identity database with a tested failover path
procedure: Stop one identity instance and sign in from an empty CLI cache. In a separate run, fail the active identity database member and repeat the test.
pass_criteria: Fresh user and service-principal sign-ins recover within the declared limit. Account and role assignments remain consistent. Revoked or invalid credentials stay denied.

scenario: Qualify and enroll a Debian host
interface: Host inventory, cloud-init, Debian package, systemd, ocean host join API
preconditions: An approved host record with a management MAC address, cell, operator pool, provisioning profile, and short-lived enrollment credential
procedure: Boot a fresh host using the inventory-generated seed. Interrupt enrollment and retry with proof of the same host key. Attempt a join with the known MAC alone, a spent credential with a different key, a failed qualification, and a revoked identity.
pass_criteria: The fresh host provisions and joins without per-host input after boot. It receives one identity and the authorized cell and pool. A retry preserves the record. Unauthenticated, replayed, unqualified, and revoked hosts receive no work.

scenario: Boot the small-node lab on trixie
interface: KVM/QEMU configuration, VDE interfaces, node inventory, and host resource metrics
preconditions: trixie with KVM access, a Debian node image, and declared host memory, CPU, and disk budgets
procedure: Start three ocean guests with 1 GiB of RAM and one vCPU each. Verify their role-appropriate management and workload attachments, join, and quorum. If required, boot a nested KVM guest and verify its workload network access.
pass_criteria: Each node has the declared allocation and its interfaces use the intended VDE segments. The three voters are healthy on the management network. The nested path works when required. The run stays within the declared host resource budgets.

scenario: Scale to 16 small ocean nodes
interface: Ocean host join and drain operations, workload CLI, placement and host metrics
preconditions: The three-node lab and the 1 GiB per-node profile, with host and support-service headroom checked
procedure: Provision additional ocean nodes from approved inventory records until 16 are enrolled and running. Inspect inventory and place a bounded mix of a small HTTP container, a stateful container, and a Functions fixture. Drain a worker and remove the added nodes after the run.
pass_criteria: All 16 nodes have real agents, unique identities, and the declared RAM allocation. Quorum membership stays at three. Eligible nodes receive work, fixture probes pass through drain, and host memory and disk use stay within the declared limits.

scenario: Exercise mixed RAM and vCPU profiles
interface: KVM/QEMU configuration, node capacity inventory, az container create, az functionapp create
preconditions: A host budget and a mixed deployment including small, workload, or separately sized support nodes
procedure: Configure at least two guest RAM and vCPU combinations. Verify effective capacity for each role and place representative workloads. Submit a request that exceeds each eligible node capacity, then run a supported workload within capacity.
pass_criteria: The hypervisor honors each node profile. Advertised capacity accounts for resources reserved by the node. Oversized requests are rejected or remain pending as documented, and supported requests complete within the declared lab limits.

scenario: Run a public Linux container from a registry
interface: az container create/show/list/start/stop/restart/logs/delete, HTTP client
preconditions: A public OCI HTTP fixture pinned by digest and a free public endpoint
procedure: Deploy with fixed CPU, memory, port, and restart settings. Observe the request response and write a known log event. Stop, start, restart, then delete the group.
pass_criteria: CLI and actual workload state agree. The HTTP response and log event are correct. The group stops serving when stopped. Deletion releases its endpoint and quota allocation.

scenario: Enforce limits and protect secret configuration
interface: az container create/show/logs, workload probe
preconditions: A fixture that records whether configuration is present without printing secret values
procedure: Start the fixture with ordinary and secure variables and declared resource limits. Exercise the limits and search inventory, audit output, and logs for the secret marker.
pass_criteria: The workload receives the declared settings. The platform enforces the documented limits. The marker is absent from inventory, audit output, and platform logs.

scenario: Mount and retain persistent container data
interface: az storage account create/show, az storage share-rm create/show, az container create with Azure Files mount parameters
preconditions: A tenant with storage provisioning rights and a workload that writes a known checksum
procedure: Create and inspect the account and share. Mount the share, write data, and restart the container. Deploy a replacement with the same authorized mount. Try to mount the share from another tenant.
pass_criteria: The original and replacement return the same checksum. The foreign tenant cannot mount or read the share. Removing the container does not remove an independently managed share.

scenario: Protect workload data at rest
interface: Storage, snapshot, backup, and key-service evidence
preconditions: A test volume with a distinctive plaintext marker and the configured encryption policy
procedure: Write the marker, create a snapshot and a backup, and verify encryption and key access at each storage boundary. Restore and read the marker with an authorized workload.
pass_criteria: The volume, snapshot, and backup are encrypted at rest under the declared policy. An unauthorized principal cannot obtain usable keys or recover the marker. The authorized restore returns the original data.

scenario: Deploy a keyed Java 21 HTTP Function
interface: az functionapp plan create/show, az functionapp create --image, az functionapp show, az functionapp function list, az functionapp function keys list/set, HTTPS client
preconditions: A Functions v4 Java 21 fixture image pinned by digest, a plan profile, and supported Function host storage
procedure: Deploy the function and list it. Set an authorized test key. Call the documented route with a valid key, without a key, and with an invalid key.
pass_criteria: The function is discoverable and the valid request returns the expected body and status. Requests without a valid key are rejected. A principal without the key-management role cannot read or change function keys.

scenario: Update and operate a Function App
interface: az functionapp config container set/show, az functionapp config appsettings set/list, az functionapp list/start/stop/restart/delete, az functionapp plan delete
preconditions: Two pinned fixture image versions with distinguishable responses and an existing Function App
procedure: Change a nonsecret app setting and update the image. Observe the new response and confirm the setting. Stop, start, and restart the app. Delete it and clean up the plan.
pass_criteria: The intended image and setting take effect. Lifecycle responses match endpoint availability. The key policy still applies after update and restart. Cleanup releases the app, its endpoint, and allocated capacity.

scenario: Create a private tenant network with firewall rules
interface: az network vnet create/show/delete, az network vnet subnet create/update/show/delete, az network nsg create/show/delete, az network nsg rule create/list/delete
preconditions: Two tenants, separate management and workload networks, and test clients inside and outside the allowed network path
procedure: Deploy a Linux group into a private subnet. Verify allowed and denied ingress and egress. From the workload network, try reaching etcd and management-only agent endpoints. Attempt private access from another tenant, then remove the resources.
pass_criteria: Allowed traffic follows the intended workload route and firewall rules. Tenant traffic cannot reach management-only services or the other tenant. CLI state reflects the effective configuration and cleanup succeeds.

scenario: Publish a private workload over HTTPS
interface: az network public-ip create/show/delete, az network application-gateway create/show/delete, HTTPS client
preconditions: A private container endpoint, test DNS, and a trusted test certificate
procedure: Associate a public IP with an HTTPS ingress gateway and target the private workload. Send a valid HTTPS request, test an unauthorized route, and remove the gateway.
pass_criteria: The public name resolves and presents the expected certificate. The allowed route returns the workload response. Disallowed routes and direct internet access to the private backend fail.

scenario: Keep a stable outbound IP for a Function App
interface: az network public-ip create/show, az network nat gateway create/show, az network vnet subnet update, az functionapp vnet-integration add/list, external IP observer
preconditions: A private subnet, a reserved public IP, and a Function App that can call the observer
procedure: Attach NAT to the subnet, integrate the app, and send requests from the function before and after a gateway failover.
pass_criteria: The observer sees the assigned public source IP before and after failover. Service resumes within the declared network recovery limit.

scenario: Deploy the network-only Bicep template
interface: az deployment group what-if, az deployment group create
preconditions: A parameterized template using the supported VNet, subnet, public IP, and NAT resources
procedure: Run what-if against a populated group, deploy the template, inspect the resulting resources, and run what-if again.
pass_criteria: The preview identifies the supported changes without mutating resources. Deployment produces the requested topology. The next preview reports no material changes.

scenario: Reach a private workload through redundant WireGuard gateways
interface: az rest against the ocean VPN API, on-premises client
preconditions: A separate customer network, two gateway instances with independent WireGuard paths, and an approved tenant prefix
procedure: Provision both tunnels. Verify permitted and denied traffic from the customer network. Stop the active gateway and measure route recovery. Verify the independent management path during the outage.
pass_criteria: The permitted route recovers over the surviving tunnel within the declared limit. Management remains reachable through its own path. Unapproved prefixes and management-only services remain inaccessible from the customer network.

scenario: Read workload health and audit events
interface: az resource list/show, az monitor activity-log list, az rest for Resource Health
preconditions: A tenant workload and a second tenant with no rights to it
procedure: Run create, update, stop, and delete actions. Cause a known health transition. Retrieve inventory, health, and activity from each tenant.
pass_criteria: Authorized results reflect actual resource state. Audit records identify actor, target, action, and outcome. The second tenant cannot read foreign records.

scenario: Measure container usage and function telemetry
interface: az monitor metrics list, az container logs, az rest for Application Insights queries
preconditions: A controlled load generator and fixtures with known successful and failing requests, an exception, and a dependency call
procedure: Run the load, query the metric and Insights windows, and compare the reported results with the test request log and resource observations.
pass_criteria: CPU and memory series, request counts, error rates, latency, exceptions, and dependency data agree with the test within declared tolerances. Data arrives within the declared delay and remains tenant-scoped.

scenario: Enforce concurrent resource limits and expose usage
interface: az rest for ACI location usage, az container create/delete, az monitor metrics list
preconditions: A tenant quota low enough to exhaust with two concurrent creates
procedure: Read the limit and current usage. Race creates that would exceed the remaining quota. Inspect reservations versus measured usage. Delete or fail the admitted resource and retry.
pass_criteria: Committed reservations never exceed the quota. Rejected operations leave no orphan allocation. Capacity becomes reusable after cleanup and the usage endpoint reports the correct limit and consumption.

scenario: Bound telemetry failure and backlog
interface: az container create and host-failure procedure, telemetry health and backlog metrics
preconditions: A running platform with a configured buffer budget and a faultable telemetry backend
procedure: Stop telemetry ingestion, generate load, provision a new workload, and exercise fencing while the backend is down. Restore ingestion and measure the backlog and lost data.
pass_criteria: Buffer use stays within budget. Provisioning and fencing complete. Reporting exposes the gap and recovers within the declared ingestion and loss limits.

scenario: Reconcile fixed counts and local autoscaling
interface: Workload lifecycle CLI, az rest against the scaling policy API, replica inventory, and load generator
preconditions: A stateless HTTP fixture, a farm with capacity on separate hosts, and declared scaling thresholds and quota limits
procedure: Apply a fixed count and vary traffic. Lose a replica and observe replacement at the desired count. Enable local autoscaling, drive scale-out and scale-in, and submit a limit that conflicts with the selected redundancy tier.
pass_criteria: Fixed mode retains its desired count through load changes and replaces failed replicas. Local mode adjusts replicas only within its allowed farm, within quota and the documented time limits. Scale-in preserves the tier minimum. Conflicting settings are rejected.

scenario: Maintain locally redundant services through a single-node failure
interface: Host fault injection, az lifecycle and login, external HTTPS probes, and storage and audit evidence
preconditions: A farm with independent logical hosts, replicated services, an allowed spare placement, persisted test data, and declared request and recovery limits
procedure: Probe each locally redundant service from outside the farm. Stop one role-bearing node at a time and restore it before the next run. Verify workload placement, fencing, persistent data, and management and identity service operations.
pass_criteria: Every logical probe of a locally redundant service succeeds within the declared client deadline and retry policy. Record per-attempt failures and latency. Single-writer recovery honors fencing, pool policy, and declared time and data-loss limits.

scenario: Fence a writer during a network partition
interface: Partition injection, write probes, storage and audit evidence
preconditions: A workload with a writable volume and a controllable path between controller, host, and storage
procedure: Partition the active host from the controller while keeping its storage path reachable. Attempt failover, then fence the writer and permit recovery. Verify writes from both placements.
pass_criteria: At most one placement can write. A lost heartbeat alone is insufficient to authorize a replacement writer. The controller records the fence outcome and resumes recovery only when it is effective.

scenario: Preserve safe behavior during quorum loss
interface: Control-plane and storage fault injection, az container show/create, live workload probes
preconditions: A healthy cell with existing workloads and separate control-plane and storage dependencies
procedure: Lose control-plane quorum in one run and storage quorum in a separate run. Attempt provisioning and writes, observe existing workloads, then restore quorum and compare state.
pass_criteria: New quorum-dependent mutations cannot commit during the outage. Existing workloads continue where the required data paths are healthy. Recovery preserves reservations and ownership without duplicate workloads or writers.

scenario: Restore metadata, tenant data, and authorized key access
interface: Backup and restore workflow, az resource show, checksum verification
preconditions: Independent backups, a known data checksum, and access to the configured key recovery path
procedure: Restore into a clean recovery environment. Verify resource ownership, workload data, authorized key access, and denial to an unauthorized environment.
pass_criteria: Recovered resources and data match the declared recovery point. Authorized workloads can access their data within the recovery limit. Unauthorized environments cannot obtain usable key material.

scenario: Fail over the regional management endpoint
interface: az account list, az group create/show/delete, external DNS and HTTPS probes
preconditions: One regional management DNS name, a virtual management IP, two gateways on the management network, and an external CLI client
procedure: Continuously resolve the management name and send authenticated requests while stopping the active gateway. Repeat for an API instance. Use the original CLI cloud configuration after each fault.
pass_criteria: The same DNS name, virtual IP, and TLS identity serve the client through the surviving gateway. Authorized reads and mutations recover within the declared endpoint limit. Retried mutations create at most one resource.

scenario: Retain management state after losing one voter
interface: az group create/show/delete, az container show, consensus and operation evidence
preconditions: Three voting members on distinct logical hosts and an acknowledged test resource
procedure: Stop the node hosting the consensus leader. Wait for a new leader. Read the acknowledged state and run a new resource mutation through the regional management endpoint. Rejoin the node.
pass_criteria: Two of three members form a quorum and accept new mutations within the declared limit. Previously acknowledged state is preserved. The rejoining member catches up without restoring an obsolete decision.

scenario: Demonstrate resilience across physical failure domains
interface: Required fault scenarios, external probes, and infrastructure evidence
preconditions: Independent physical domains and a predeclared load, latency, failover, and data loss profile
procedure: Repeat the management endpoint, identity, gateway, host, partition, quorum, and restore tests under the declared load. Test loss of an upstream network path and one authoritative DNS endpoint from outside the region. Remove a physical failure domain and separately perform a rolling maintenance update.
pass_criteria: The measured results meet the published limits. Tenant isolation, stable egress, persistent data, and fencing guarantees hold during the required failover and maintenance scenarios.

scenario: Measure workload and API performance under load
interface: Load generator, az lifecycle operations, HTTP probes, and telemetry
preconditions: A documented release topology and numerical thresholds for concurrency, throughput, and latency
procedure: Run concurrent provisioning and representative sustained HTTP traffic for both workload types. Measure tail latency, error rates, capacity, and telemetry delay across the declared steady-state period.
pass_criteria: Measured throughput, API and workload latency, errors, and time to observe telemetry meet the release thresholds. Quota enforcement and tenant isolation continue under load.

scenario: Provision a physical server from rack to ready
interface: Trusted asset inventory, out-of-band provisioning, Debian installer, ocean host join API
preconditions: A preconfigured rack, an approved unprovisioned server, and a second machine with an unapproved or mismatched identity
procedure: Rack, cable, and power on the approved server. Observe discovery, commissioning, Debian installation, agent enrollment, and qualification. Reboot the enrolled host and present the unapproved machine.
pass_criteria: The approved server reaches ready with its assigned IP, DNS name, pool, and identity without per-server configuration. A normal reboot uses the installed system. The unapproved machine remains outside the workload pool.

scenario: Operate an Azure-compatible site-to-site connection
interface: az network vnet-gateway create, az network local-gateway create, az network vpn-connection create/show/delete
preconditions: The IPsec compatibility profile is enabled and a real IPsec peer is available
procedure: Create the gateways and connection with the supported options. Establish the tunnel with the peer, verify authorized routing and connection status, and delete it.
pass_criteria: The peer interoperates using the documented IPsec profile. Traffic and CLI status agree. Teardown removes the route and tunnel access.

scenario: Deploy and promote a Functions package
interface: az functionapp deployment source config-zip, az functionapp deployment slot create/list/swap/delete when slots are enabled
preconditions: The ZIP profile is enabled and a prebuilt supported Functions package is available
procedure: Upload the package, wait for deployment and trigger availability, and invoke the function. If the slot profile is enabled, deploy a second version to a slot and swap it.
pass_criteria: The expected package version handles authorized requests. A failed deployment surfaces an error. An enabled slot swap changes the production version according to the documented settings policy.

scenario: Report monetary totals by resource and meter
interface: az rest for Microsoft.CostManagement/query
preconditions: The Cost Management profile is enabled with a known usage dataset and rate schedule
procedure: Query known date windows and group by resource and meter. Compare the returned dimensions, currency, and totals with the reference calculation.
pass_criteria: The documented table shape and totals agree with the reference within the declared rounding policy. Queries do not expose information across tenants.

scenario: Pair four farms and maintain services through mesh and farm failures
interface: WireGuard gateway mesh, route observations, federation mTLS API, local ARM probes
preconditions: Four simulated farms with three nodes each, separate quorums, two gateway nodes per farm, approved peer identities, and a geo-redundant HTTP fixture
procedure: Pair the farms automatically through the mesh. Enroll a fourth node in each farm. Probe local and geo services from outside the mesh with both fresh and cached DNS answers. Fail one node, one tunnel path, and then one entire farm in separate runs. Restore and replay pairing. Attempt an unapproved route and peer join.
pass_criteria: Each authorized pair forms one durable relationship. The 16-node run retains three voters per farm. Local probes survive node loss and geo probes survive farm loss within the declared client policy. Approved routes recover within the limit and unauthorized peers and prefixes are rejected.

scenario: Recover an authorized workload across physical sites
interface: Federation placement, storage replication and fencing evidence, independent access probes
preconditions: Physically independent sites with mesh uplinks, a geo-redundant externally reachable service, and an authorized stateful workload with a documented recovery point
procedure: Probe the geo-redundant service continuously with fresh and cached DNS answers during a WAN partition and then complete loss of one site. Verify replication and effective fencing before a stateful replacement writes. Attempt ownership transfer to an unapproved site or without proof of fencing.
pass_criteria: Each surviving site retains local control. Every geo-redundant service probe completes within policy through site loss, including clients that cached the endpoint before the fault. Stateful recovery meets declared time and data-loss limits with at most one writer. Unsafe or unauthorized transfers are held.

scenario: Autoscale within authorized farms
interface: Scaling policy API, federation placement state, regional metrics, and external load probes
preconditions: A paired four-farm lab, a geo-redundant HTTP fixture, approved target farms, and per-farm resource quota and replica minimums
procedure: Apply sustained demand and inspect scale-out across approved farms. Remove demand and verify scale-in. Inject a WAN partition and retry cross-farm reconciliation. Attempt placement in an unapproved farm.
pass_criteria: Geo autoscaling respects authorized farms, quotas, minimum live placement, and failover capacity. Retries preserve one allocation per replica. Cross-farm changes wait when authoritative placement cannot be determined.

scenario: Join a Debian client to the lab Samba AD domain
interface: realm join, adcli testjoin, PAM and Kerberos probes
preconditions: Disposable two-farm KVM lab and a digest-identified Debian image
procedure: Discover the controller through directory DNS. Synchronize time, reject an invalid join, join the domain, reboot, and sign in with the domain user. Probe the directory from the other farm.
pass_criteria: The Debian guest retains membership and resolves the expected group. PAM authentication and Kerberos succeed. The other farm cannot discover or reach the directory.

scenario: Join Windows Server 2025 Core to the lab Samba AD domain
interface: Add-Computer, Test-ComputerSecureChannel, whoami and klist
preconditions: Disposable Server Core KVM guest installed from operator-supplied Microsoft media
procedure: Discover the controller, check clock offset, reject a wrong-domain join, join the test domain, and reboot. Verify machine trust and a fresh employee session.
pass_criteria: The verified build is Server 2025 Core. Machine trust survives reboot. The employee session has the expected domain group and a Kerberos ticket.

scenario: Join Windows 11 to the lab Samba AD domain
interface: Add-Computer, Test-ComputerSecureChannel, whoami and klist
preconditions: Disposable Windows 11 Pro or Enterprise Evaluation KVM guest with official media, UEFI and TPM 2.0
procedure: Discover the controller, check clock offset, reject a wrong-domain join, join the test domain, and reboot. Verify machine trust and a fresh employee session.
pass_criteria: The verified build is Windows 11 Pro or Enterprise Evaluation. Machine trust survives reboot. The employee session has the expected domain group and a Kerberos ticket.

scenario: Bootstrap, synchronize and fault-test a Samba controller pair on one lab host
interface: Rootless Podman, DNS, Kerberos, LDAP, SMB and Samba DRS
preconditions: Local controller image, two private volumes and an isolated fixture network
procedure: Verify DNS stays closed until each controller confirms the established SID. Attempt to start the established primary using an empty volume. Create an employee before joining the replica and compare identity. Add a group membership on each controller. Update a GPO through SMB and the directory, add a custom deny ACE to a policy file, and compare the results on the replica. Restart the replica with the primary stopped, revoke a membership on the replica, then restart the primary to check revocation. Stop the replica and repeat the client checks. Remove the stopped replica and clean its Samba AD metadata. Join a replacement with an empty volume and stop the primary again.
pass_criteria: An empty primary volume cannot recreate an established directory. Memberships converge within 45 seconds in each direction and after the primary restarts. The new GPO bytes, LDAP version, and ACL converge within 65 seconds and survive a replica restart with the primary stopped. The unprivileged employee cannot access the protected file or replication export, and an administrator cannot write to replica SYSVOL. Fresh clients use DNS, Kerberos, and SMB on either survivor. The local health probe returns the established domain SID. Cold restart retains the employee SID and GUID. The replacement has a new controller account GUID, retains domain identity, and serves replicated membership, policy bytes and ACLs.

scenario: Verify the managed-directory management API and readiness response
interface: az rest PUT, GET and POST
preconditions: Unmodified Azure CLI 2.93.0 and the loopback HTTPS contract fixture with a signed tenant token
procedure: Check authorization and resource status projections through the API. Replay a provisioned directory request, read its status and submit the replica and primary fence envelopes and read a fenced recovery through the pinned CLI.
pass_criteria: The fixture rejects unauthorized requests and invalid fence envelopes, distinguishes pending, available, degraded and unavailable, and retains the completed provisioning state during outages. CLI replay and read preserve the initial directory ID and return the two ready controller endpoints.

scenario: Validate fenced replacement and writer promotion against regional state
interface: Regional etcd, Ed25519 fence proof and certified host assignments
preconditions: Disposable etcd endpoint and simulated host identities, liveness and power attestations
procedure: Reject a live replica, an expired proof, an invalid signature and the wrong generation. Admit a valid proof after liveness is removed, confirm Samba cleanup as the survivor, and race replacement scheduling after an eligible host becomes available. Fence the current writer with a distinct signed action. Probe writer-task availability before and after a fresh survivor observation and acknowledgement. Fence both current slots for paired recovery. Exercise recovery placement with insufficient capacity, then with two spare hosts.
pass_criteria: The old generation is revoked. No replacement is published before cleanup acknowledgement. The new generation keeps the address, uses another eligible host, preserves tenant capacity accounting and accepts the established SID. Retrying the proof and acknowledgement preserves the same result. Writer work and the old slot stay blocked until the new writer acknowledges promotion. The former writer returns on a spare host as a replica with a new generation. Old delegations are revoked, the standby waits for the recovered writer, and regional writes resume only after both new controllers report the original SID.

scenario: Restore a lost Samba domain from an encrypted backup into a fresh volume
interface: Samba online backup and native database recovery, OpenSSL CMS, DNS, Kerberos, LDAP, SMB and Samba member trust
preconditions: Samba controller pair on an isolated rootless Podman network and an independent backup artifact
procedure: Join a Samba member, stage a separate authorization, and add test memberships and a protected policy. Encrypt a portable backup and remove both source controllers and their volumes. Reject damaged input and recover in a disconnected container. Start the recovered controller after SID authorization and test DNS, machine trust, memberships and policy.
pass_criteria: The new controller serves the original domain SID, employee and member account GUIDs, memberships and GPO version, bytes and custom deny ACE. The Samba member authenticates with its original machine credential without rejoining. A fresh employee obtains a Kerberos ticket and cannot read the guarded policy file. Recovery revokes the outstanding join authorization before its original expiry.

scenario: Join one prestaged Debian machine using a scoped temporary AD principal
interface: Samba directory ACLs, Kerberos and Debian adcli
preconditions: Isolated Podman controller and a digest-identified Debian join client image
procedure: Stage a computer and retry the same authorization. Try to adopt its name with another authorization. Try the delegated account against a different existing machine and a new name. Join the intended computer and verify its keytab. Close the used authorization, then attempt another join. Obtain a ticket before a separate authorization expires and repeat after expiry.
pass_criteria: The matching request yields the same identity before it is used. Other machine joins and re-staging a used authorization fail. The intended machine authenticates with its keytab. Closing is idempotent and removes the join account's ACEs. A fresh ticket is refused after expiry and the cleanup worker removes the expired ACEs.

scenario: Issue and close an actual machine join authorization with az rest
interface: Azure CLI 2.93.0, regional etcd, mTLS node enrollment, rootless Samba and Debian adcli
preconditions: Disposable etcd and digest-identified Samba and Debian client images
procedure: Reject a non-administrator, a foreign tenant, unauthorized hosts and a stale acknowledgement. PUT and replay a join request. Verify the bounded encrypted queue, run the certified node agent, and read the result. Try to close before a client joins. Complete a Debian join and retry closing with the CLI. The provisioned scope uses one live controller.
pass_criteria: The CLI reports Pending then Ready, and the job is delivered only to the active writer generation. The password is absent from the public response and plaintext store. An early close leaves the credential active. The joined client verifies its machine trust. The CLI reports Closed and the old login fails on the real controller.

scenario: Manage Samba workforce users through stock az ad user
interface: Azure CLI 2.93.0, Graph v1.0, etcd, mTLS node enrollment, Samba and Kerberos
preconditions: Disposable etcd and digest-identified Samba and Debian client images
procedure: Create a workforce user, filter by UPN and display-name prefix, and show the object by UPN and GUID. Verify a fresh ticket in the Debian fixture, rotate the password and repeat the request with the new credential. Update the display name and disable the user. Verify protection of the built-in Samba administrator and rejection of an ARM token at Graph.
pass_criteria: Operations return the same AD object GUID. The display name and status changes are visible through Graph and preserve the alias. The initial and rotated passwords obtain fresh tickets at their respective checks. A new ticket request fails after disable. The built-in administrator remains outside the managed user scope.

scenario: Manage AD security groups with stock az ad group and verify access
interface: Azure CLI 2.93.0, Graph v1.0, etcd, mTLS node enrollment, Samba, Kerberos and SMB
preconditions: Disposable etcd and digest-identified Samba and Debian client images
procedure: Create, replay, list and read a security group. Compare the Graph GUID to the native AD group and its SID. Restrict a disposable SMB share to the AD group. Reject a foreign member URL and a user outside the managed workforce. Add and remove the managed user, replay both changes, and list memberships. Reopen a fresh Debian Kerberos SMB session at each stage.
pass_criteria: The CLI replays the same security group GUID and reports the native membership changes. The fresh SMB client is denied before membership, reads the expected bytes after membership, and receives Access Denied after removal.

scenario: Promote the surviving Samba controller and replace the failed writer
interface: Samba FSMO, Kerberos, SMB and Podman
preconditions: Digest-identified Samba controller image and rootless Podman on one host
procedure: Join a Samba member and stop DC01. Demonstrate that a SYSVOL version mismatch blocks promotion while the survivor stays readable. Restart DC02 with the promotion generation, confirm its original SID, and check all FSMO owners. Write a new policy version and member group. Join a new DC01 on an empty volume, compare identity, policy bytes and ACL, and retry the promotion after DC01 has joined.
pass_criteria: DC02 owns the seven FSMO roles. Fresh Kerberos, existing machine trust and policy access succeed. The replacement serves the new GPO and its ACL with policy writes denied. Replayed promotion preserves the new DC01 machine account.

scenario: Rebuild a Samba AD controller pair from an independent backup
interface: Samba domain backup, Kerberos, SMB, OpenSSL and Podman
preconditions: Digest-identified Samba controller image, rootless Podman and OpenSSL on one host
procedure: Back up a controller and encrypt the verified archive. Delete both original volumes, reject corrupt input and an unauthorized startup, and restore a writer on an empty volume with a rotated bootstrap credential. Replay the assigned restore and reject a different digest. Join a fresh standby with the rotated credential and stop the recovered writer.
pass_criteria: The standby serves the existing member's secure channel and employee Kerberos, preserving the domain SID, account GUIDs, groups, SYSVOL policy bytes, version and exact ACL. Administrator policy writes on the standby are denied. The old administrator credential and outstanding delegations are revoked.

scenario: Recover existing Windows members through the regional directory workflow
interface: Azure CLI 2.93.0, etcd, mTLS node agents, KVM and native Windows probes
preconditions: Independent Samba backup and two joined Windows KVM fixtures, two disposable Debian KVM hosts, and isolated etcd
procedure: Submit the signed source-slot fence to the regional API. Stage the archive on the assigned writer. Wait for real agent enrollment, offline restore and the standby join. Verify both Windows members, power off the recovered writer guest, and run fresh client probes against the survivor.
pass_criteria: The regional API reports Succeeded when both replacements serve the original SID and Degraded after writer loss. Both Windows machines retain their trust and preserved policy, and fresh employee sessions obtain Kerberos and the original group.

scenario: Verify Windows sign-in and SMB access after regional Graph changes
interface: Azure CLI 2.93.0, etcd, mTLS node agents, Samba, KVM, Windows Server Core
preconditions: The isolated recovery hosts and archive from WORKPLACE-14, and one existing Windows Server Core member
procedure: Create and read a workforce user and group with az ad. Exercise member add, list and remove, password rotation and account disable. Run fresh Windows logon probes between mutations.
pass_criteria: Native identities match the Graph GUIDs. Windows obtains a fresh CIFS ticket, is denied the group share before membership, reads the expected data with membership, and loses access after removal. Windows rejects the old and disabled credentials.

scenario: Provision a new per-tenant AD domain on packaged hosts and exercise either controller outage
interface: Stock Azure CLI 2.93.0, regional ARM, etcd, Debian agent package, Samba and KVM
preconditions: Two disposable enrolled Debian guests with the agent package and Samba image, and a separate Debian client
procedure: Submit and replay the directory request, inspect status and deny foreign and unauthorized requests. Verify both routed private controllers. Power off each host separately, test the survivor, and restart the stopped host.
pass_criteria: One directory becomes available on two hosts. Fresh DNS, Kerberos and SMB reads through the packaged network return the same SYSVOL file with either host off. API status converges to Degraded and back to Available using the same placements.

scenario: Register distinct web application callbacks through Graph
interface: Stock Azure CLI 2.93.0 and Graph v1.0
preconditions: Disposable loopback etcd and signed tenant test identities
procedure: Register two single-tenant applications with separate HTTPS callback sets. Replay one registration and try to replace its callback on replay. Reject a wildcard callback, inspect the retained values, reject automation credentials for web applications, and register an automation application using its existing request shape.
pass_criteria: Each app has its own object and client IDs. Replay preserves IDs and exact callbacks. Failed requests leave the registered callback set unchanged, and automation registration remains available.

scenario: Prepare isolated native OIDC clients for Graph registrations
interface: Keycloak 26.8.2 Admin REST and OIDC
preconditions: Disposable Keycloak with trusted HTTPS and an admin service account
procedure: Create a tenant realm and prepare the OIDC clients for two distinct web registrations. Replay preparation, attempt a callback and registration ownership change, and check collisions with an existing automation client. Send an authorization request with S256 and the registered callback before policy publication.
pass_criteria: The prepared clients have distinct identities, exact callbacks and a dedicated browser-flow binding. Replays are stable and security settings are verified. Authorization fails while disabled, and automation retains its original service account.

scenario: Read Samba workforce identities and memberships through Keycloak
interface: Keycloak 26.8.2 Admin REST and OIDC, Samba AD and LDAPS
preconditions: Disposable Samba replica pair and a Keycloak instance with the lab LDAPS trust root
procedure: Verify both controller binds and reject an invalid reader credential. Prepare the tenant federation twice. Validate the LDAP user and group IDs, exclude accounts outside the managed scope and confirm the local tenant administrator. Stop the primary, obtain a fresh signed token through the standby and repeat the lookup. Restart the primary, remove the group membership, reject a write through the LDAP reader, re-add the membership, and disable and re-enable the user.
pass_criteria: The two controllers preserve the same native GUIDs and Keycloak subjects. Keycloak rejects sign-in from outside the managed scope and after AD account disable. The next lookup reflects group changes, and replay while degraded leaves the original provider and mapper IDs intact.

scenario: Register two apps with Azure CLI and exercise one Samba-backed MFA session
interface: Stock Azure CLI 2.93.0, Graph v1.0, ARM 2026-11-01, Keycloak 26.8.2, Chromium, LDAPS and OIDC
preconditions: WORKPLACE-19 fixtures, trusted HTTPS, a fresh administrator CLI cache and a clean browser profile without a domain ticket
procedure: Sign in with device code, register both clients through Graph and apply distinct managed AD group GUIDs through ARM. Reject foreign and malformed policy, incompatible redirects, plain PKCE and an out-of-scope user. Sign in through Chromium with a workforce password and TOTP, then reuse the session in the second app, then remove its group membership and recreate the group under its old name.
pass_criteria: Both CLI-registered clients issue signed, app-specific audiences for the same subject and MFA session. Revocation denies the affected app a new code while the first app retains access. A recreated group cannot inherit the original grant.

scenario: Use a Samba service ticket in a fresh Debian Firefox profile
interface: Stock Azure CLI 2.93.0, ARM 2026-11-01, Samba Kerberos, Firefox ESR and Keycloak 26.8.2
preconditions: WORKPLACE-19 fixtures with private HTTP service keytab, employee credential cache and trusted HTTPS
procedure: Prepare the LDAP provider, add web Kerberos through policy activation and replay, and inspect the default browser binding. Start a fresh Firefox profile configured for the issuer. Verify the authorization code and signed token. Disable the Samba account and probe the existing token at UserInfo and a fresh Kerberos authorization request.
pass_criteria: Firefox uses the Samba ticket and returns an authorization code without interactive credentials. Its token has the existing AD user's subject, the expected app audience and assurance. The default browser flow keeps SPNEGO disabled. Account disable rejects new authorization and the old token at live UserInfo before its nominal expiry.

scenario: Preserve fresh CLI workflows when a tenant enables web Kerberos
interface: Stock Azure CLI 2.93.0, device-code and service-principal OAuth, ARM and Graph
preconditions: WORKPLACE-19 fixtures and a private HTTP service keytab
procedure: Run separate device-code and automation sign-ins for an existing tenant and a tenant eligible for federation. Check subscription and Graph access. Activate web Kerberos through the managed administrator's CLI, then repeat with fresh caches.
pass_criteria: Both tenants keep the same verified administrator and service principal subjects. ARM discovery returns only the assigned subscription. Graph reads the tenant-owned application and denies foreign applications and non-administrators. ARM rejects Graph tokens.

scenario: Sign in from a joined Debian PAM session with Firefox
interface: Stock Azure CLI 2.93.0, ARM 2026-11-01, Samba AD, SSSD PAM, Firefox ESR and Keycloak
preconditions: Joined Debian guest, two Samba controllers, private keytab and a DNS issuer
procedure: Activate a web policy through the ARM endpoint. Verify the machine join and open a fresh PAM domain-user session. Start a clean Firefox profile with the issuer CA and SPNEGO origin, then exchange the authorization code.
pass_criteria: PAM provides the employee TGT. Firefox acquires the HTTP service ticket into that cache without entering a browser password. Signed OIDC tokens preserve the mapped directory subject, application audience and assurance.

scenario: Sign in from a joined Windows desktop session with Edge
interface: Stock Azure CLI 2.93.0, ARM 2026-11-01, Samba AD, Windows 11, Edge and Keycloak
preconditions: Joined Windows desktop session, two Samba controllers, private keytab and verified HTTPS
procedure: Activate the Kerberos web policy. Check the interactive Windows domain account and its TGT. Start a fresh Edge profile with integrated authentication enabled and verify the HTTPS callback and new service ticket.
pass_criteria: Edge uses the existing Windows logon to acquire an AES HTTP service ticket without entering browser credentials. Signed OIDC tokens preserve the mapped directory subject, application audience and assurance.

scenario: Verify Kerberos admission to a private SMB member
interface: Debian smbclient, Samba AD, SMB 3 encryption and the member audit trail
preconditions: Joined Debian guest, directory member on a tenant address, LUKS2 ext4 share, test accounts and a guest on the foreign network
procedure: Write and compare content using a personal CIFS ticket, then read it as a different user. Attempt a read-only write, an ungrouped tree connect, a password-only login and a foreign network connection. Remove the write group membership and request a fresh TGT.
pass_criteria: The content matches. No denied client gains access beyond its grant. The journal records the native writer and reader identities. The group change denies a session with a fresh TGT within 20 seconds.

scenario: Enforce the share quota and file locks on an encrypted RBD volume
interface: Linux CIFS with Kerberos and SMB 3.1.1 encryption, Samba member, LUKS2 and replicated Ceph RBD
preconditions: WORKPLACE-25 lab, project quota on the member's dedicated RBD volume and two independent client SMB connections
procedure: Write and flush files concurrently over both connections, and read each other's data. Attempt a write that crosses the combined budget. Lock a byte from one connection and attempt the same lock from the other before and after releasing it.
pass_criteria: Both acknowledged writes are readable. The shared filesystem refuses writes past its quota. A conflicting lock is rejected and can be acquired after the holder releases it.

scenario: Manage the lifecycle and ACL of a Kerberos SMB share with Azure CLI
interface: Stock Azure CLI 2.93.0, Ocean.Storage 2026-11-01, enrolled Debian Samba member, and replicated Ceph RBD
preconditions: Private managed domain fixture, installed Ocean agent package, test regional etcd and Ceph storage
procedure: Create and replay a pending share request. Reject foreign groups, subscription access and an unauthenticated host plan read. Poll the certified worker's publication, verify actual Kerberos access, change the ACL, and verify the acknowledged file after the update. Request deletion and poll it.
pass_criteria: The same request keeps the volume and operation. The ACL changes on the same encrypted volume and the prior reader is denied. The completed delete removes the projection, listener, mount and RBD image. The resource group cannot delete a live share implicitly.

scenario: Use one AD identity from Windows Server Core and Debian
interface: Personal Kerberos tickets, Windows SMB, Debian smbclient and the Samba member journal
preconditions: Joined Windows Server Core and Debian guests, WORKPLACE-25 accounts, and a common encrypted share
procedure: Write and flush a new nonce file from a Windows writer session. Read it as a Windows reader and attempt a write. Attempt to read it as an ungranted Windows account. Read the nonce from Debian as the original writer and inspect both clients in the journal.
pass_criteria: Windows obtains a CIFS ticket for each domain user. The expected grants control actual file access. Debian reads the same acknowledged bytes and the audit log records the same writer from both client addresses.

scenario: Recover a Kerberos SMB share after confirmed writer fencing
interface: Stock Azure CLI 2.93.0, enrolled Samba members, Debian CIFS, KVM, and replicated Ceph RBD
preconditions: Two enrolled SMB hosts in one cell and private subnet, a floating address, encrypted Samba state and share volumes, and a lab signing authority
procedure: Flush a file and hold its descriptor and byte-range lock. Isolate the primary's management path. Check that its lease expires and the standby receives no storage grant. Hard-stop the primary, reject a forged fence, and submit and replay the signed fence. Reconnect with Kerberos, read the flushed bytes, check the old descriptor, and acquire a lock on a fresh open. Reboot the former owner.
pass_criteria: The lease loss leaves the old member as the sole writer. The valid proof changes the generation once. Reconnection uses the same Kerberos endpoint and preserves the acknowledged bytes. A fresh open can lock and flush a write. The old descriptor's behavior is recorded. The old owner returns without the IP, mapped storage or a new grant.

scenario: Restore a tenant SMB share from independent backups
interface: Stock Azure CLI 2.93.0, ocean-recover, authenticated etcd snapshot, encrypted Ceph RBD exports, Windows Server Core and Debian Kerberos
preconditions: WORKPLACE-29 fixture, healthy joined Windows and Debian clients, and an independent restore pool and metadata cluster
procedure: Write and flush a checkpoint, set an individual file ACL, stop the writer and export its share and Samba state as ciphertext. Save metadata independently. Stop the source metadata cluster, restore a new cluster, and import only the backups using an isolated pool. Reject cross-tenant and wrong-key recovery. Reopen the share with its original ID and rerun native Kerberos access from Debian and Windows.
pass_criteria: The replacement has a separate cluster identity and cannot access the source pool. The published share keeps its native identity, file ownership, ACLs and hard quota. Both clients read the acknowledged bytes, readers cannot write and an ungranted account cannot read. Backup hashes and elapsed times are recorded.

scenario: Provision and operate a private Windows Server 2025 Core guest
interface: Stock az rest, enrolled Debian KVM worker, replicated Ceph RBD and private guest probe
preconditions: Digest-pinned Windows image and firmware, isolated regional etcd and the installed Debian worker package
procedure: Register the image and private NIC. Create the VM and replay the request. Inspect the VM, NIC and disk, reject foreign subscription reads and deletes, and verify the lack of a TCP management listener on QEMU. Stop, restart and delete the guest. Record the runs and quota observations.
pass_criteria: The Windows NIC responds at its assigned address. The CLI matches runtime power state. Replay preserves the reservation. CPU, memory and disk stay charged while stopped and return to zero after deletion. Foreign requests cannot read or mutate the resources.

scenario: Recover an acknowledged Windows disk write after worker fencing
interface: Stock az rest, SMB 3, regional fence API, out-of-band lab power control and Ceph mappings
preconditions: Two enrolled KVM workers, three separate storage guests, a disposable encrypted SMB checkpoint fixture and the lab fencer public key
procedure: Write and read a random SMB checkpoint. Partition the current worker from management and wait for its lease to expire. Count host assignments and writable disk maps, then stop the original worker through the external supervisor and submit a signed fence. Read the checkpoint, guest identity and boot record on the replacement. Reboot the retired worker.
pass_criteria: A partition alone leaves exactly one writer. A forged fence fails and replaying a valid fence is safe. The recovered VM uses the same private address, disk, system UUID and Windows identity with fresh boot evidence and the exact checkpoint bytes. The returning worker has no assignment or writable disk map.
